purpose: How a GPS/fleet-tracking reseller keeps and grows the recurring side of the business after installation: managing per-unit subscription margin as a mechanism computed from the operator's own invoices, keeping installed devices healthy and their data credible, holding billing, platform seats, and contract terms in reconciled order, reading fleet-account churn signals months before renewal, and expanding inside accounts with more vehicles, assets, dashcams, and modules only through lawful, disclosure-current, evidence-grounded motions.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a small GPS/fleet-tracking reseller running an installed base of tracked units across SMB fleet accounts (trades, delivery, trucking, equipment rental) on a third-party tracking platform whose seats the reseller pays for wholesale
units enter this KB already installed, verified per unit, and on billing - the installation and onboarding handoff is complete before any node here fires
accounts were originally sold under employer authorization with driver disclosure completed at intake; this KB is responsible for keeping that state current, not creating it

every dollar amount, rate, margin, or percentage in this KB is a mechanism (how the number comes to exist and how to compute it from the operator's own ledger and platform invoice) or a qualitative band, never an asserted market fact
exclusions: fleet segment targeting, prospect qualification, reseller-versus-white-label channel economics, and new-logo offer and pricing design - the market-and-economics KB owns that territory

device selection per use case, physical installation, concealment-versus-serviceability trade-offs, initial platform configuration of geofences, alerts, and reports, initial driver-disclosure onboarding, and per-unit verification testing at install - the installation-and-onboarding KB owns that territory; this KB begins after a unit is installed, verified, and billing
covert tracking of private individuals, or any tracking outside owner or employer-authorized vehicles and assets - such requests are refused and documented, never managed as business

asserting jurisdiction-specific ELD, hours-of-service, or telematics-privacy rules as settled fact - obligation classes are named and flagged with a verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction note instead

invented per-unit prices, margins, churn rates, benchmark comparisons, or account multiples stated as fact - all economics appear as mechanisms computed from the operator's own numbers or as qualitative bands
personalized financial, legal, tax, or insurance advice to the operator or to the operator's customers

competency_questions.question: What does one tracked unit actually earn and cost each month in my book, and where does per-unit margin silently leak?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNIT_MRR_LEDGER defines the per-unit revenue and cost line structure as a mechanism from the operator's own price sheet and platform invoice, PLAN_TIER_MODULE_MAP shows how tier mix moves the margin, and SEAT_COST_RECONCILIATION names the leak mechanisms (orphan seats, ghost units, mid-cycle wholesale changes)

competency_questions.question: How do I keep an installed base honest - which units are silent, mis-assigned, or reporting implausible data - before the customer notices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEVICE_HEALTH_TELEMETRY gives the exception-list method with per-device-class silence windows and failure signatures, and DATA_QUALITY_AUDIT gives the assignment, plausibility, and geofence-currency checks that certify which data may be cited

competency_questions.question: How do I know whether the humans at a fleet account still use the platform, and what does usage decay predict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USAGE_ENGAGEMENT_TELEMETRY defines engagement scoring across logins, report consumption, and alert response, counts passive consumption channels, and names usage decay as the earliest churn precursor

competency_questions.question: When a unit goes dead, what is the cheapest path back to reporting, and when is a technician visit actually justified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_SERVICE_TRIAGE lays out the remote-first ladder (remote diagnostics, guided self-check, mail-swap, truck roll last) with batching rules, and SUPPORT_LOAD_ECONOMICS supplies the per-path cost mechanism that justifies or blocks the visit

competency_questions.question: How do I plan for hardware failure batches and cellular network sunsets without eating the whole swap cost at once?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RMA_SWAP_AND_SUNSET_PLANNING covers spare pools, advance replacement, batch-defect detection, and sunset campaigns amortized across renewal cycles, and CONTRACT_TERM_REGISTER supplies the renewal dates the campaign is scheduled against

competency_questions.question: What keeps support cost per unit from eating the subscription margin as the installed base grows?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPORT_LOAD_ECONOMICS gives the tickets-per-hundred-units mechanism with cause tagging and below-water account detection, and ALERT_RETUNE_CYCLE shows how killing alert noise removes a major upstream ticket driver

competency_questions.question: How do billing, dunning, and suspension work on fleet accounts without torching relationships that could be kept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BILLING_HYGIENE_DUNNING defines invoice-to-ledger reconciliation before send, a published dunning ladder, and suspension design that separates report access from recovery-relevant function

competency_questions.question: What must the contract register capture so a renewal never arrives as a surprise and subsidized hardware is never stranded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACT_TERM_REGISTER lists term, notice window, auto-renew status, co-terming rule, and the subsidy-recovery balance mechanism, and derives the renewal calendar worked backward from notice windows

competency_questions.question: How do I run a renewal conversation grounded in the account's own recorded value, without inventing a single savings figure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_PLAYBOOK gives the pre-window preparation, fix-before-ask discipline, and mechanism-explained repricing; ACCOUNT_HEALTH_REVIEW supplies the health brief and value-event log; DATA_QUALITY_AUDIT certifies which data the recap may cite

competency_questions.question: Where is the expansion whitespace in each account, and what must be true before I propose dashcams, asset trackers, or new modules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_WHITESPACE_MAP inventories tracked-versus-total with readiness states, EXPANSION_MOTION requires the health gate and the lawful-use gate before any ask, LAWFUL_USE_STANDING_GUARD defines the authorization and disclosure preconditions, and REGULATORY_DRIFT_WATCH forces jurisdiction verification for recording-capable device classes

competency_questions.question: Which churn signals actually precede fleet-account losses, and how do I decide save, restructure, or release?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_SIGNAL_WATCH catalogs the trade's signals (engagement decay, champion departure, payment slowdown, fleet downsizing, repeat tickets) with watch-tier routing, and SAVE_AND_WINBACK_RULES matches the save tool to the diagnosed driver with concessions bounded by support-cost tier

competency_questions.question: How does fleet composition change - vehicles bought, sold, wrecked, trackers moved - stay synchronized with billing, platform seats, and disclosure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLEET_TURNOVER_SYNC defines the turnover intake path, transfer and deactivation procedures that update ledger, seat, invoice, and authorization scope together, and SEAT_COST_RECONCILIATION proves the sync worked via the three-way count

competency_questions.question: What book-level view tells me whether the recurring base is growing healthily, and what do I fix first when it is not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_MRR_GATE defines the movement ledger with unit, account, and cause attribution, the growth-quality overlay from support tiers, and the decision pass that assigns owners to the next period's fixes

competency_questions.question: Which account requests must be refused outright during the account lifecycle, even at the cost of the account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAWFUL_USE_STANDING_GUARD names the refusal classes (tracking private individuals, suppressing disclosure, units outside authorization scope) with documentation of each refusal, and EXPANSION_MOTION and SAVE_AND_WINBACK_RULES show the guard binding growth and retention pressure alike

glossary.definition: The monthly recurring revenue attached to one active tracked unit - its retail subscription line for a given plan tier and modules; summed over active units it is the book, and its margin is the retail line minus the wholesale platform seat cost minus allocated support overhead, always computed from the operator's own numbers.

A platform seat the reseller keeps paying wholesale for although no customer is billed against it any longer - typically left behind when a vehicle was sold or a unit died and the deactivation never reached the platform; the classic silent margin leak.

A unit still billed to a customer although the device has been dead or removed for months; when discovered by the customer it converts into a multi-month credit demand and lasting distrust of every future invoice.

A tracker that stopped reporting without any alarm - unplugged OBD device, cut power, drained asset-tracker battery, dead cellular coverage, or a sold vehicle; surfaced by exception lists ranked on last-report age rather than by customer complaints.

The monthly three-way comparison of seats the platform bills the reseller, units the reseller bills customers, and devices actually alive on vehicles; per-unit margin only exists after the three counts agree or every delta is explained.

The published escalation sequence for overdue accounts - reminder, personal contact, service restriction, suspension - with each rung's timing stated in the terms so collection is predictable rather than improvised per account.

Aligning the subscription end date of units added mid-term with the account's master renewal date, so the account renews as one decision on one date instead of fragmenting into per-unit anniversaries.

A cellular carrier retiring a network generation on a published date, which permanently kills every tracker built on that modem class and forces a fleet-wide hardware swap campaign - best amortized across renewal cycles rather than absorbed as one emergency.

An account whose devices report perfectly while no human logs in or reads the reports; it renews only until someone reviews the invoice, which is why engagement telemetry, not device health, is the leading churn indicator.

Dispatching a technician to a vehicle or yard - the most expensive support action per incident, capable of consuming months of one unit's subscription margin, and therefore reserved for the last rung of the remote-first triage ladder.

nodes.definition: Maintain the ledger that treats every installed, billing tracker as one recurring line item: which vehicle or asset it rides on, which customer account owns it, which plan tier and modules it carries, its activation date, its contract-term linkage, the retail subscription billed to the customer, and the wholesale platform seat cost the reseller pays beneath it. Per-unit margin is a mechanism - retail line minus wholesale seat cost minus an allocated slice of support and billing overhead - computed from the operator's own price sheet and platform invoice, never quoted as an industry figure. The ledger is the substrate every other motion reads: health monitoring maps device to line, billing maps line to invoice, renewal maps lines to terms, and the book gate sums movements across them.

included: unit-level revenue and cost line structure
activation and deactivation states per unit
plan and module tagging per unit
margin-as-mechanism computation from the operator's own invoices
excluded: setting new-logo prices and offer design
the platform's own invoice format
install and verification records from onboarding

pros.claim: A unit-level ledger makes every MRR movement attributable - each dollar of growth or shrinkage traces to a named unit on a named account
pros.example: a five-unit contraction showing as five identified deactivated vans on one landscaping account instead of an unexplained revenue dip

cons.claim: Unit-level bookkeeping is real overhead at scale and drifts from reality the moment field changes go unrecorded
cons.example: a tracker moved from a sold pickup to its replacement still ledgered against the old VIN three months later

failure_modes: running the book on account-level totals so churn and expansion can never be attributed to units
letting activation dates diverge from billing start dates so proration disputes multiply
acceptance_tests: every active device on the platform maps to exactly one ledger line carrying plan tier, retail line, wholesale seat cost, and contract linkage
revisit_triggers: the platform changes its seat or licensing structure
the operator adds a new device class or module family to the book

base.update_signal: the platform's seat billing structure or the operator's own plan sheet changes shape

nodes.definition: Keep the lawful-tracking boundary enforced for the life of the account, not just at the sale: tracking stays confined to vehicles and assets the customer owns or controls as an employer, employee disclosure remains current as drivers, vehicles, and device classes change, and requests that drift toward covert tracking of private individuals - a tracker for a spouse's personal car, an employee's own vehicle without disclosure, a unit the drivers must not know about - are refused and documented regardless of the MRR at stake. The guard runs at known trigger points: fleet turnover events, expansion asks, save conversations, and any request to suppress or delay disclosure.

included: disclosure currency checks at turnover and expansion
refusal classes with documentation of each refusal
escalation when a customer self-activates units outside scope
excluded: the initial driver-disclosure onboarding session
adjudicating the customer's internal HR disputes
legal advice on a specific dispute - refer to counsel

pros.claim: Refusing bright-line requests early costs one unit of MRR and avoids the account-and-reputation loss of a covert-tracking incident
pros.example: declining to activate a tracker a customer bought for a former partner's car, and noting the refusal with its trigger on the account record

cons.claim: The guard adds friction to legitimate growth and can misread lawful edge cases involving mixed personal use
cons.example: a take-home company van whose after-hours tracking needs the employer's written personal-use policy, not a reflex refusal

failure_modes: treating the intake disclosure as permanent while the driver roster turns over completely
letting a customer self-activate units on vehicles outside the recorded authorization scope unnoticed
acceptance_tests: every account carries a current authorization scope and disclosure status, every refusal is documented with its trigger, and no active unit sits outside the recorded scope
revisit_triggers: a customer requests a device class with new privacy stakes such as a driver-facing camera or audio capture
a turnover event adds vehicles or drivers not covered by the recorded disclosure

base.update_signal: a refusal case, disclosure gap, or new device class exposes a hole in the guard's trigger list

nodes.definition: Track which accounts sit in regulated classes - fleets that may fall under ELD and hours-of-service mandates, jurisdictions with telematics or workplace-privacy rules, consent regimes for driver-facing cameras and in-cab audio - as obligation classes with a verification flag, never as asserted specifics. The rules are jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific and they drift: a fleet crosses an operating threshold, a privacy statute lands, a platform module adds recording. The watch names the class, records why the account is flagged, and forces verification of current rules in the customer's jurisdiction before any renewal commitment or module expansion leans on a compliance claim.

included: drift triggers: fleet-type change, jurisdiction change, module change
excluded: asserting current ELD or privacy specifics as fact
compliance consulting or legal advice
sale-time regulated-class qualification of new prospects

pros.claim: Flagging obligation classes instead of memorizing rules keeps every compliance-touching motion honest even as regimes change under it
pros.example: a renewal note reading that the customer added interstate lanes so ELD applicability must be re-verified, instead of a stale remembered verdict

cons.claim: Constant verification flags slow decisions and can frustrate customers who want a straight compliance answer
cons.example: a trucking owner pressing for a yes-or-no on an ELD module and receiving a verification path plus a counsel referral instead

failure_modes: asserting a remembered rule that has since changed and anchoring a renewal commitment on it
missing that an account's operations drifted into a regulated class mid-term
acceptance_tests: every flagged account names the obligation class, the reason for the flag, and the jurisdiction-verification note, and no renewal or expansion artifact asserts a specific current rule
revisit_triggers: a customer's operations change fleet type or jurisdiction
a module with recording or telematics-privacy implications is proposed for any account

base.update_signal: a regulatory change notice lands, or a verification finding contradicts a recorded flag

nodes.definition: Watch the whole installed base as an exception list: units ranked by last-report age, GPS fix quality, power events, and battery state, so silent units surface within a defined reporting-gap window instead of being discovered by the customer. Failure signatures differ by device class - an OBD unit going dark usually means unplugged or vehicle sold, a hardwired unit losing power events suggests an ignition-circuit fault, a battery asset tracker declines along a battery curve toward scheduled replacement rather than breaking suddenly. The customer pays monthly for data; a dead unit is a refund conversation waiting to happen and the fastest silent killer of renewal credibility.

included: last-report exception dashboards across the base
silence-window thresholds set per check-in cadence
proactive customer notification of dead units
excluded: initial per-unit verification testing at install
the repair action itself
platform-wide outage management, which belongs to the vendor

pros.claim: Catching a silent unit inside the window turns a churn grievance into a proactive service touch the customer remembers at renewal
pros.example: calling the fleet manager about a dark unit on a skid steer before its owner discovers the gap during a theft scare

cons.claim: Exception thresholds tuned too tight flood the operator with false alarms from parked vehicles and coverage dead zones
cons.example: a seasonal landscaping trailer flagged dead every winter although it is merely parked inside a metal barn

failure_modes: monitoring only what customers complain about, so silence accumulates unseen across the base
using one silence window across device classes whose check-in cadences differ by an order of magnitude
acceptance_tests: the exception list covers every active unit, silence windows are set per device class, and each silent unit has an owner and a next action inside the operator's stated response window
revisit_triggers: a device class or firmware cohort changes its reporting behavior
the silent-unit rate shifts materially after an install-practice change

base.update_signal: silent-unit or false-alarm rates move after a threshold, firmware, or install-practice change

nodes.definition: Audit the quality of the data the subscription actually sells, beyond mere device liveness: trackers assigned to the right vehicle names, odometer and engine-hour values plausible against service records, geofences still matching the customer's current yards and job sites, duplicate or retired assets purged, and drivers mapped where driver-level reporting is sold. Quality erodes invisibly through fleet change: a tracker swapped between vehicles keeps its old label, a moved depot leaves geofence alerts firing on an empty lot. Because renewal recaps and expansion arguments are only as honest as this data, the audit ends by certifying which account data is fit to cite in front of the customer.

excluded: initial geofence, alert, and report configuration
device liveness itself
the customer's operational data hygiene outside the tracking platform

pros.claim: Certified-clean data makes every downstream value claim defensible in front of the customer's own staff
pros.example: an idle-time trend the fleet manager can reconcile against his dispatch log because every vehicle label is right

cons.claim: Audits at unit scale are tedious, easy to defer, and over-auditing wastes hours on cosmetic issues no report consumes
cons.example: perfecting asset labels for a customer who only ever opens the live-map view

failure_modes: a renewal recap built on mislabeled vehicles collapsing when the customer spots a truck he sold last year in the data
geofence alerts firing on an abandoned yard until the customer learns to ignore every alert
acceptance_tests: each account passes the audit checklist - assignment, plausibility, geofence currency, duplicates - on the operator's cadence or carries an open exception with an owner
revisit_triggers: a fleet turnover event lands on the account
an alert-noise complaint or a value-recap dispute traces back to stale data

base.update_signal: audit exceptions cluster on one cause - turnover, label drift, geofence staleness - prompting a checklist or cadence change

nodes.definition: Instrument whether humans at the account still consume what the devices produce: login recency by user, scheduled-report opens, alert acknowledgment, mobile-app use by dispatchers, and which features - live map, history replay, maintenance reminders - actually get touched. Devices reporting flawlessly to an audience of zero is the classic zombie account: it renews only until someone reads the invoice. Engagement telemetry converts that invisible decay into a leading indicator months before the renewal window, and identifies the single-user dependency where one departure would orphan the whole platform at the account.

included: login, report, and alert consumption tracking
excluded: initial user training at onboarding
the customer's internal management practices
using usage data to surveil individual drivers beyond the employer's disclosed program

pros.claim: Usage decay is the earliest reliably observable churn precursor and costs almost nothing to instrument from platform admin views
pros.example: spotting that a nine-truck plumbing outfit's dispatcher has not logged in for sixty days while every device stays green

cons.claim: Raw login counts mislead because some healthy accounts consume value passively through emailed exception reports and never log in
cons.example: an owner who reads only the weekly idle-report email being scored as disengaged and pestered into annoyance

failure_modes: reading device health as customer engagement and missing the zombie account entirely
scoring passively-consuming accounts as at-risk and spending retention effort where none is needed
acceptance_tests: every account carries an engagement score combining logins, report consumption, and alert response, with passive consumption channels counted before any account is scored disengaged
revisit_triggers: churn post-mortems show the engagement score missed or mis-weighted a signal
the platform changes what usage telemetry its admin views expose

base.update_signal: the correlation between engagement scores and actual renewal outcomes in the operator's own book contradicts the current weighting

nodes.definition: Run a remote-first triage ladder for units flagged unhealthy: remote diagnostics and reboot commands from the platform first; then a guided customer self-check - is the device seated, has the vehicle moved, is the fuse intact; then a mail-swap with a pre-provisioned replacement and a return label; and only last a technician visit, because a truck roll is the most expensive support action per incident and can consume months of that unit's subscription margin - a mechanism the operator prices from their own labor and travel cost, never a quoted figure. The ladder also decides batching: a single dead unit waits for the next scheduled visit window, while a cluster at one yard justifies one combined trip.

included: triage ladder order and exit criteria per rung
per-path cost mechanism from the operator's own labor numbers
excluded: new-install workmanship standards
warranty terms with the hardware vendor
pricing service plans into the customer offer

pros.claim: Most dead-unit causes clear at the remote or self-check rung, reserving field labor for genuine hardware faults
pros.example: half a fleet's dark OBD units restored by walking a foreman through reseating devices after a round of battery changes

cons.claim: Pushing self-service too hard on a paying fleet reads as shirking and burns goodwill on accounts that expect full service
cons.example: a flagship trucking account asked to fuse-test its own hardwired units souring weeks before its renewal

failure_modes: rolling a truck for what a remote reboot command fixes
sending mail-swaps without capturing the failed unit back for diagnosis and warranty
acceptance_tests: every dead-unit ticket shows the ladder rungs attempted in order, and every truck roll records why remote paths were exhausted or deliberately skipped
revisit_triggers: the mix of root causes shifts across a firmware or install cohort
customer-tier expectations change what level of self-service is acceptable

base.update_signal: resolution rates by ladder rung shift, changing where triage effort should concentrate

nodes.definition: Manage the hardware layer of the installed base as inventory risk: a spare pool sized to the observed failure pattern of each device class; an advance-replacement flow so a customer's vehicle is not waiting weeks on a vendor RMA cycle; capture and vendor-return of failed units under warranty terms; batch-defect detection so a firmware cohort draining batteries is treated as a campaign, not a stream of unrelated tickets; and planning for cellular network sunsets, which retire an entire modem generation on a date and force fleet-wide swap campaigns best amortized across renewal cycles rather than absorbed as one emergency. Swap economics are mechanisms - hardware cost, vendor credit, labor path, any customer contribution negotiated at renewal - never a quoted standard price.

included: warranty capture and vendor RMA handling
sunset swap campaigns scheduled against renewal dates
excluded: initial device-class selection per use case
vendor contract negotiation
pitching the sunset as a new-prospect sales angle

pros.claim: Sunset campaigns planned against the contract register convert a forced cost into a hardware-refresh renewal story
pros.example: spreading modem-generation swaps across a year of renewal windows with loaner units covering early failures

cons.claim: Spare pools and advance replacements tie up cash in hardware that may be obsolete before it ships
cons.example: a shelf of spare units for a model the vendor end-of-lifed before the spares were consumed

failure_modes: learning about a network sunset from customer outage calls instead of carrier notices
replacing batch-defect units one ticket at a time without ever noticing the cohort
acceptance_tests: spare-pool levels are set per device class from observed failure patterns, every sunset-affected unit is inventoried with a swap window, and failed units are captured for warranty and cohort analysis
revisit_triggers: a carrier sunset announcement or vendor end-of-life notice lands
a failure-rate step change appears in one hardware or firmware cohort

base.update_signal: carrier or vendor lifecycle notices, or cohort failure data, change the swap plan

nodes.definition: Treat support cost per unit as the quiet variable that decides whether the subscription book compounds or erodes: the mechanism is tickets per hundred units per month, times minutes per ticket, times loaded labor cost, plus the truck-roll tail - all computed from the operator's own logs, never quoted as an industry norm. The drivers are identifiable and fixable upstream: install-quality cohorts surfacing as repeat power tickets, alert misconfiguration, untrained new staff at the customer, and device classes with high failure signatures. The node's discipline is attribution - every ticket tagged by cause and account - so the operator knows which accounts and cohorts sit below water, feeding save-or-release decisions and pacing expansion.

included: deflection via self-serve guides and customer-admin training
excluded: setting support pricing or service levels in the offer
fixing install workmanship itself - this node only routes the evidence back
the triage ladder mechanics

pros.claim: Cause-tagged tickets turn support from a cost blur into an upstream repair list
pros.example: discovering one electrical contractor generates a third of all tickets because every new apprentice trips the same misconfigured geofence alarm

cons.claim: Rigorous tagging is discipline-heavy for a small operator, and sloppy tags are worse than none
cons.example: a catch-all device-issue tag hiding that most tickets were actually training questions with a documentation fix

failure_modes: averaging support cost across the book and missing that two accounts consume the margin of twenty
treating rising ticket volume as demand for more staff instead of a symptom to fix upstream
acceptance_tests: tickets carry cause and account tags, per-account support tiers exist, and below-water accounts are flagged to the book gate with their evidence
revisit_triggers: ticket volume or cause mix shifts across two consecutive cycles
a new device class or module changes the support surface

base.update_signal: the operator's own ticket logs contradict the assumed cost drivers or the per-account tier boundaries

nodes.definition: Re-tune alerts and reports on a cycle after onboarding, because the configuration that fit the fleet at install decays as the fleet changes: speed thresholds set for city vans misfire when highway routes are added, geofences outlive moved yards, after-hours alerts fire on a newly added night shift. Alert fatigue is a double killer - it generates support tickets and it trains users to ignore the platform, which later reads as usage decay. The cycle reviews firing counts per alert, kills or repairs the top noise sources with the customer in the room, and confirms that the alerts which matter to this fleet's workflow still reach a human who acts on them.

included: noise-source repair sessions with the customer
confirmation that actionable alerts reach an owner
retune cadence tied to fleet-change events
excluded: the initial alert and report configuration to the fleet's workflow
alert behavior the platform does not expose for tuning
disciplining the customer's staff for ignoring alerts

pros.claim: Killing the top noise sources measurably restores both alert response and platform trust
pros.example: silencing a defunct yard's geofence alarm and watching the fleet manager start answering after-hours-movement alerts again

cons.claim: Retuning needs customer time, and repeated sessions can feel like the product was never set up right
cons.example: a third tuning request in one quarter prompting the owner to ask why this keeps needing adjustment

failure_modes: leaving install-time thresholds untouched for years while the fleet's operating pattern changed underneath them
tuning noise down so far that a genuine theft-movement alert is disabled with the junk
acceptance_tests: each account shows a retune record on cadence or after fleet-change events, with firing counts before and after the top noise fixes
revisit_triggers: alert-driven tickets spike on an account
a fleet-change event lands - new routes, moved yards, added shifts - or a real event slips through ignored

base.update_signal: firing-count and response data show the current thresholds no longer fit the fleet's operating pattern

nodes.definition: Keep the monthly invoice unarguable and the collection path predictable: invoices reconcile line-for-line to active ledger units before they are sent, mid-cycle adds and removals are prorated by a stated rule, plan changes take effect on a stated boundary, and overdue accounts walk a dunning ladder - reminder, personal contact, service restriction, suspension - with each rung's timing published in the terms rather than improvised per account. Suspension mechanics need special care in this trade: cutting tracking on a fleet mid-dispute also cuts theft-recovery capability, so the ladder distinguishes restricting reports and logins from disabling recovery-relevant location function, and never silently deactivates platform seats that are expensive to re-provision.

included: the published dunning ladder with rung timing
suspension design separating report access from recovery-relevant function
excluded: initial payment terms and pricing design
collections litigation and credit reporting - refer out
waiving arrears as a retention tactic, which the save rules decide explicitly

pros.claim: An invoice that always matches the observable fleet removes the most common trigger of billing disputes and churn-by-annoyance
pros.example: a controller spot-checking three VINs against invoice lines, finding all three right, and paying without a phone call

cons.claim: A rigid ladder can escalate on a good account in a temporary cash pinch and convert a savable situation into an exit
cons.example: a seasonal excavation firm suspended in its slow month after three years of flawless payment

failure_modes: invoicing for units that were removed from vehicles months earlier
improvising suspension per account so customers learn the terms are negotiable through delay
acceptance_tests: pre-send reconciliation passes with zero unexplained line deltas, and every overdue account sits on a documented ladder rung with its next action dated
revisit_triggers: billing-dispute volume ticks upward
a suspension case exposes a gap between report restriction and recovery-relevant function

base.update_signal: dispute or involuntary-churn patterns show a ladder rung or proration rule misfiring

nodes.definition: Maintain the map of which units carry which plan tier and which paid modules - base track-and-trace, higher-frequency ping plans, dashcam channels, maintenance-module seats, ELD-related modules where lawfully applicable - because tier mix is where per-unit MRR is actually made and lost. The map records each tier's wholesale cost and retail line as the operator's own mechanism, which module entitlements each account actually uses (feeding both whitespace and downgrade honesty), and the upgrade and downgrade mechanics: effective-date boundaries, proration treatment, and whether the platform meters a module per unit, per account, or per user. An entitlement paid for but unused is a downgrade conversation or an adoption repair waiting; either beats the customer discovering it at renewal.

included: tier and module assignment per unit
excluded: designing the tier catalog and its pricing
functional setup of modules on the platform
compliance assertions about regulated modules, which the drift watch flags

pros.claim: An accurate tier map turns renewal and expansion pricing into arithmetic on known lines instead of account archaeology
pros.example: quoting a dashcam add-on for exactly the eight tractors already on the premium ping plan without re-auditing the account

cons.claim: Fine-grained tiering multiplies billing states and error surface at small-operator scale
cons.example: three tier variants inside one account producing a proration defect every time a vehicle transfers

failure_modes: selling a module the customer already pays for on another tier
leaving units on legacy tiers whose wholesale cost quietly rose above the retail line
acceptance_tests: every unit carries a tier and module tag matching both the platform entitlement and the invoice line, with unused entitlements flagged
revisit_triggers: the platform repackages its tiers or modules
the entitlement-usage review shows systematic non-adoption of a paid module

base.update_signal: platform repackaging or the usage review changes what tiers and modules the map must represent

nodes.definition: Reconcile, on a monthly cycle, three counts that drift apart in the real world: seats the platform bills the reseller (wholesale), units the reseller bills customers (retail), and devices actually alive on vehicles (physical). Every mismatch is a named leak with a mechanism: an orphan seat still costing wholesale after a vehicle was sold; a ghost unit billed to a customer but dead for months - a refund and trust bomb; a seat provisioned for a swap that never got decommissioned; a wholesale price change landing mid-cycle. Per-unit margin only exists after this reconciliation, which is why the inputs are always the operator's own counts and invoices, never assumed rates, and the closed report feeds the book gate with the true recurring cost base.

included: three-way count reconciliation on a monthly cycle
leak attribution to cause with close-out actions
excluded: negotiating wholesale terms with the platform
the deactivation policy itself, which turnover sync owns
customer refund decisions above the operator's stated threshold - owner call

pros.claim: The monthly reconciliation habitually recovers real margin that silently leaks at unit scale
pros.example: finding a dozen orphan seats from last year's fleet downsizing still accruing wholesale cost every month

cons.claim: Three-way reconciliation is exacting clerical work that small operators skip under load, which is exactly when leaks grow fastest
cons.example: deferring reconciliation through a busy install quarter and absorbing months of seats for returned rental equipment

failure_modes: paying wholesale indefinitely for seats no customer funds
discovering ghost units only when the customer demands a multi-month credit
acceptance_tests: the monthly report shows zero unexplained deltas across the three counts, and every explained delta carries a cause tag and a close-out action
revisit_triggers: the platform changes its seat billing or deactivation semantics
turnover volume makes the current reconciliation cadence insufficient

base.update_signal: reconciliation deltas or platform billing changes shift where the leak mechanisms live

nodes.definition: Keep a register of every account's contractual skeleton: term start and end, auto-renew and notice-window clauses, the co-terming rule for mid-term unit additions, any hardware subsidy being recovered inside the term with its remaining-balance mechanism, price-adjustment rights, and early-termination mechanics. The register drives a renewal calendar worked backward from notice windows, because a missed window either locks an unwanted auto-renewal - breeding resentful churn later - or lets a term lapse silently to month-to-month, dissolving the recovery of subsidized hardware. Subsidy recovery is a mechanism: hardware cost spread against the term's subscription margin per the operator's own deal sheet, never a standard figure.

included: renewal calendar worked backward from notice windows
excluded: designing term lengths and subsidy structures for new deals
the renewal conversation itself
enforcing termination fees in a dispute - refer to counsel

pros.claim: A notice-window calendar makes every renewal a prepared campaign instead of a surprise found in an inbox
pros.example: a ninety-day-out flag triggering the health review and recap build for a fifteen-vehicle roofing fleet

cons.claim: Register discipline decays with every hand-edited amendment and side agreement unless changes are logged at signing
cons.example: a verbally extended term nobody wrote down surfacing as a dispute exactly at the register's recorded end date

failure_modes: auto-renew lapsing an account into month-to-month with subsidized hardware unrecovered
co-termed additions inheriting a renewal date nobody communicated to the customer
acceptance_tests: every account shows term, notice window, auto-renew status, and subsidy-balance mechanism, and no renewal date sits inside its notice window without an owner and a planned motion
revisit_triggers: an amendment or side agreement lands on any account
a subsidy-recovery balance goes negative against the remaining term

base.update_signal: term amendments, missed-window incidents, or subsidy-balance anomalies expose register gaps

nodes.definition: Run a lightweight periodic review per account - the SMB-fleet cousin of a quarterly business review - assembling device health, data-quality certification, engagement trend, support-ticket profile, and recorded value events (recovered assets, geofence catches, idle-time trends the customer's own data shows) into one health brief with a tier: healthy, watch, or intervene. The brief is the single artifact renewal and expansion both read, which forces its honesty: it cites only audit-certified data, it names problems the operator caused - dead units, noisy alerts - as plainly as customer-side decay, and it ends with the one next action that most changes the account's trajectory.

included: value-event log drawn from the account's own data
excluded: the renewal or expansion conversation itself
inventing savings the data does not show
deep financial analysis of the customer's business

pros.claim: One recurring brief prevents renewal-time archaeology and makes every account conversation start from shared facts
pros.example: opening a renewal with the customer's own two recovered-trailer events and the quarter's dead-unit fix history

cons.claim: Reviews at book scale compete with billable work and degrade into checkbox exercises when over-templated
cons.example: twenty consecutive all-good briefs signaling that the review stopped actually looking

failure_modes: briefs that hide operator-caused problems and lose all credibility when the customer knows better
health tiers assigned by gut feel instead of the assembled evidence
acceptance_tests: each account has a brief current on cadence, citing only certified data, carrying a tier with its evidence and one named next action
revisit_triggers: an account's tier changes in either direction
a value event or incident lands that the next brief must carry
a renewal enters its notice window

base.update_signal: assigned health tiers diverge from actual renewal and churn outcomes

nodes.definition: Run renewals as a prepared motion that starts well before the notice window: the health brief supplies the value recap - recovered assets, resolved tickets, usage the customer actually got - expressed in the account's own recorded events, never invented savings; open problems such as dead units or stale geofences are fixed or owned with a dated plan before the ask; price changes are explained by mechanism - wholesale movement, tier mix, hardware refresh at a sunset - rather than asserted; and term options are offered honestly, including month-to-month where lock-in would only manufacture resentment. A renewal earned on demonstrated value renews again; one extracted through an auto-renew technicality churns later with prejudice and takes referrals with it.

excluded: new-logo ROI selling
compliance assertions inside the recap - the drift watch flags those for verification
win-at-any-price discounting, which the book gate and support economics bound

pros.claim: Fix-before-ask converts the renewal meeting from a price negotiation into a continuation decision
pros.example: replacing two dead units and silencing a noisy alarm the month before the ask, then opening the meeting with exactly that

cons.claim: Heavy preparation on every renewal over-invests in small stable accounts that would have renewed on a two-line email
cons.example: building a full recap deck for a three-unit landscaper already on autopay

failure_modes: leading with a discount instead of value and teaching the account to negotiate every year
citing an efficiency claim the customer's own data does not support and losing the room
acceptance_tests: every renewal shows a pre-window preparation record, a recap citing only certified account events, open problems owned with dates, and any price change explained by a named mechanism
revisit_triggers: renewal outcomes shift - close rate, concessions demanded, term mix
a recap dispute traces back to data or claim quality
wholesale or sunset mechanics change the repricing story

base.update_signal: renewal outcomes and dispute causes in the operator's own book contradict the playbook's emphasis

nodes.definition: Keep the tracked estate synchronized with the customer's actual fleet as vehicles are bought, sold, wrecked, and reassigned: a stated intake path for turnover events - customer notification backstopped by operator detection when a unit goes dark in a sold vehicle; a transfer procedure that moves a tracker to the replacement vehicle with its label, geofence relevance, and driver assignment updated; a deactivation procedure that ends retail billing and the wholesale seat together; and a disclosure check whenever a transfer puts units on vehicles or drivers outside the recorded authorization scope. Unsynced turnover is the single upstream cause behind ghost units, orphan seats, mislabeled data, and invoice disputes - which is why this node feeds reconciliation rather than duplicating it.

included: turnover-event intake path with detection backstop
transfer procedure updating label, geofence relevance, and driver assignment
deactivation that closes billing and platform seat together
authorization and disclosure check on every transfer
excluded: the physical re-installation work
the reconciliation arithmetic itself
advising the customer on fleet purchase decisions

pros.claim: A single turnover procedure closes the root cause of most billing and data-quality leaks in one move
pros.example: a sold box truck's tracker transferred to its replacement the same week, with ledger, label, and invoice all moving together

cons.claim: The procedure depends on customers reporting sales the operator cannot always observe, so detection must backstop notification
cons.example: an equipment-rental account that sells attachments at auction without telling anyone until the units go dark

failure_modes: billing a customer for a tracker riding in a wrecked vehicle at a salvage yard
transferring a unit onto a new driver's vehicle with the disclosure never refreshed
acceptance_tests: every turnover event shows an intake record and a completed transfer or deactivation, with ledger, platform seat, invoice, and authorization scope updated together
revisit_triggers: dark units cluster in a pattern suggesting unreported vehicle sales
an account's turnover volume outgrows the intake path

base.update_signal: leak post-mortems repeatedly attribute causes to turnover-intake gaps

nodes.definition: Score fleet accounts continuously on the churn signals this trade actually exhibits: engagement decay while devices stay green, the champion - fleet manager or dispatcher - leaving, payment behavior slowing, fleet downsizing, unresolved or repeating support tickets, a competitor's name surfacing in conversations, and renewal-adjacent silence. Signals are weighted from the operator's own loss history - a mechanism recalibrated by post-mortems, never a borrowed benchmark - and accounts roll up into watch tiers that route attention: healthy accounts keep the standard cadence, watch accounts get a scheduled human touch, intervene accounts get an owner and a plan before the notice window arrives.

excluded: the save action itself
manufacturing urgency or fear to re-engage an account
surveilling the customer beyond ordinary business signals

pros.claim: Tiered watch converts churn from a renewal-day ambush into a months-early queue of workable problems
pros.example: a dispatcher's departure flagged the week it happened, triggering a re-training touch that kept the account

cons.claim: Signal scoring on a small book overfits, and one noisy signal can flood the watch tier with false positives
cons.example: a single slow-payment month during a customer's known seasonal trough tripping a full intervention

failure_modes: watching device dashboards while the human relationship decays invisibly
scoring signals but routing no owner, so watch tiers become a graveyard of unread flags
acceptance_tests: every account carries a current tier from the signal scorecard, and every watch or intervene account names an owner and a next dated touch
revisit_triggers: a churn post-mortem contradicts the current signal weighting
the book's composition changes - a new segment or size class enters

base.update_signal: post-mortems and save outcomes show which signals actually preceded losses in this book

nodes.definition: Decide save, restructure, or release with rules set before the emergency: diagnose the churn driver first - price, unused value, service failure, fleet shrinkage, ownership change - then match the tool to the driver: adoption help for unused value, a fix-and-make-good for service failure, a downgrade or unit-count reduction for shrinkage, a term restructure for price; and bound every concession by the account's support-cost tier so a save never manufactures a below-water account. The ethics are first-class: no fear-selling - no invented theft statistics to scare a fleet into staying; no concealing that a downgrade exists; no punitive friction on exit - offboarding is clean, data export honored, the door left open, because released accounts that shrink to fit sometimes return grown, and winback timing keys to the competitor's first renewal or service stumble.

included: clean-exit offboarding with honored data export
excluded: dunning mechanics
fear-based retention tactics - prohibited outright, not merely out of scope
re-acquisition offers designed for new logos

pros.claim: Driver-matched saves cost less and hold longer than reflex discounts
pros.example: saving a shrinking excavation fleet by cutting to eight units and pausing two, instead of discounting all fourteen

cons.claim: Rules written for the median case can be too slow for a top account walking over a solvable service failure
cons.example: a flagship trucking account needing a same-day make-good while the process asks for a diagnosis form first

failure_modes: discounting every threat and training the whole book to threaten
retaining chronic below-water accounts because releasing feels like failure
acceptance_tests: every save case records the diagnosed driver, the matched tool, and the concession's bound against the support tier, and every release shows a completed clean-exit checklist
revisit_triggers: save outcomes - hold rate, re-churn - contradict the rules
a winback signal fires on a released account

base.update_signal: hold-rate and re-churn outcomes of past saves reveal which tools actually work for which drivers

nodes.definition: Maintain per account an inventory of what is tracked versus what could lawfully be: untracked vehicles visible in the customer's own fleet count, trailers and yellow iron carrying no asset trackers, module gaps that fit the fleet's workflow - dashcams for accounts with incident exposure, the maintenance module where breakdowns drive tickets - and entitlements owned but unused, which are adoption repairs rather than upsell targets. Every whitespace entry carries a readiness state, because whitespace is a fact while an expansion ask is a decision: an account with dead units or a watch tier has its whitespace frozen until health recovers, and every entry notes the authorization and disclosure implication of the device class involved.

included: authorization implication note per device class
excluded: making the expansion ask itself
prospect-level whitespace of non-customers
inflating fleet counts beyond what the customer disclosed

pros.claim: A standing whitespace map makes expansion a harvest of recorded facts instead of a periodic brainstorm
pros.example: knowing at renewal time that eleven of a rental account's thirty attachments carry no asset tracker

cons.claim: A map maintained without readiness discipline becomes a pushy call list that erodes trust
cons.example: pitching dashcams to an account midway through an unresolved dead-unit complaint

failure_modes: whitespace built from guessed fleet sizes the customer never disclosed
treating unused entitlements as upsell targets instead of adoption repairs
acceptance_tests: each account's map lists tracked-versus-total by class, module gaps, a readiness state, and the authorization note per entry
revisit_triggers: a turnover event changes the fleet's composition
a value event makes a whitespace entry newly arguable
a health-tier change flips readiness

base.update_signal: expansion outcomes show which whitespace classes convert and which asks were premature

nodes.definition: Execute expansion asks - more vehicles, asset trackers on trailers and equipment, dashcams, maintenance or other modules - as evidence-triggered motions: the trigger is an event in the account's own data such as a recovered asset, a new-vehicle purchase, or an incident a dashcam would have settled; the proposal cites that recorded event and prices by the operator's own tier mechanism; added units co-term onto the master renewal date; and installation hands off to the operator's install practice rather than being improvised. Two gates precede every ask: the health gate - no expansion into an account with dead units or a watch tier - and the lawful-use gate - authorization scope covers the new units, and disclosure is refreshed for new device classes, driver-facing cameras above all, where consent and recording rules are jurisdiction-specific and must be verified before proposing, not after installing.

included: the health gate and the lawful-use gate
verification-first rule for recording-capable device classes
excluded: the physical install and configuration
new-logo selling
fear-framed pitches - an incident is cited as the customer's own recorded event, never dramatized

pros.claim: Expansion sold on the account's own recorded event closes without discounting because the evidence belongs to the customer
pros.example: covering the remaining trailers after the account's own recovered-trailer event, priced straight from the existing tier map

cons.claim: Waiting for perfect evidence can idle obvious whitespace for quarters
cons.example: an account that bought six vans in January not hearing an ask until a triggering event in June

failure_modes: expanding into an account with unresolved dead units and converting goodwill into a bigger grievance
activating driver-facing cameras before consent rules were verified and disclosure refreshed
acceptance_tests: every ask records its triggering account event, both gate checks - health and lawful-use with disclosure - the co-terming treatment, and tier-mechanism pricing
revisit_triggers: expansion win rate or post-expansion account health shifts
a new device class changes the gate checklist
a jurisdiction verification changes what may be proposed

base.update_signal: expansion outcomes and gate incidents show which triggers and checks actually protect the account

nodes.definition: Close the loop at book level on a fixed cadence: an MRR movement ledger sorting the period's change into new units, expansion, contraction, and churn - each movement attributed to named units, accounts, and causes rather than reported as a net blur; the support-cost tiers overlaid so growth quality is visible, not just growth; and a decision pass assigning the next period's attention - which watch accounts get owners, which leaks get closed, which cohorts get root-caused, which below-water accounts get restructured or released. The gate's definition of done is attributability: a period closes only when every movement has a cause and every red flag has an owner, and its honesty rule is that book metrics are the operator's own arithmetic, never dressed up against invented industry baselines.

included: movement ledger with unit, account, and cause attribution
decision pass assigning owners and actions
excluded: acquisition strategy behind the new-unit line
presenting book performance to lenders or investors as advice
benchmark comparisons asserted as fact

pros.claim: Cause-attributed movement turns the book from a number that happened into a set of levers with owners
pros.example: a flat quarter decomposing into strong expansion masked by one fleet downsizing, which changes the response entirely

cons.claim: Full attribution discipline at every close is heavy for a solo operator and tempting to skip in good quarters
cons.example: a growth quarter closed unattributed, hiding the churn cohort that surfaces the following period

failure_modes: managing to net MRR and missing that churn is being papered over by expansion
closing periods with unexplained movements that compound into an unauditable book
acceptance_tests: each period close shows every movement attributed to unit, account, and cause, the growth-quality overlay present, and each flag assigned an owner with a dated action
revisit_triggers: attribution reveals a recurring upstream cause - install cohort, turnover intake, alert noise
the book's shape changes enough to re-weight the decision pass

base.update_signal: period-close attributions repeatedly trace to causes the gate's decision pass under-weights

edges.why_related: the drift watch extends the standing lawful-use guard into jurisdiction-specific obligation classes that must be verified rather than asserted
health monitoring maps each device exception back to the ledger line whose revenue it endangers
data quality is only auditable on units that are alive; the audit starts from the health exception list
engagement is scored per account against the units and entitlements the ledger says the account pays for
the triage ladder consumes the health exception list as its work queue
hardware planning sizes spare pools and detects cohorts from the failed units triage captures back
support economics prices each triage path and consumes the ticket stream triage generates
declining alert response and logins are what trigger and target a retune session
the invoice is reconciled line-for-line against active ledger units before it is sent
tier and module tags attach to the ledger's unit lines and refine their revenue and cost mechanisms
assignment and label anomalies found by the audit are how unreported turnover is detected
every transfer procedure includes the guard's authorization and disclosure check before a unit moves
reconciliation compares wholesale seat charges against the tier map's expected cost per unit
completed transfers and deactivations are the ground truth the three-way count is checked against
each ledger line carries its contract linkage, and the register aggregates those linkages into terms and windows
the health brief opens with device-health status because dead units invalidate every other claim in it
the engagement trend is the brief's second pillar, separating zombie accounts from healthy quiet ones
the renewal motion is scheduled backward from the register's notice windows
the health brief supplies the value recap and the fix-before-ask problem list the renewal runs on
engagement decay is the heaviest-weighted signal in the churn scorecard
payment-behavior changes surfaced by the dunning ladder feed the churn scorecard as a signal
save decisions consume the watch tier and signal history as their diagnosis input
module gaps and unused entitlements in the tier map are half the whitespace inventory
turnover events reveal untracked additions to the fleet that become whitespace entries
every expansion ask draws its target and readiness state from the whitespace map
the health gate that precedes every ask reads the brief's current tier
renewal outcomes are the retention movements the book ledger attributes and closes
expansion outcomes are the growth movements the book ledger attributes and quality-checks
the reconciled cost base is what makes the gate's margin and growth-quality overlay honest
expansion revenue pressure pushes toward activating units and device classes faster than authorization scope and disclosure can be verified
edges.resolution_rule: the guard wins absolutely: no unit or device class activates until authorization scope covers it and disclosure is refreshed, and a request to track private individuals is refused and documented regardless of the deal size

edges.why_related: deep concessions that save an account can pin it permanently below the support-cost floor
edges.resolution_rule: the support-cost tier bounds every concession: an account that cannot be saved above the floor is restructured to fewer units or a lighter tier, or released cleanly - never retained at a loss to avoid admitting the loss

edges.why_related: the dunning ladder's scheduled escalation can suspend exactly the account the save motion is trying to keep
edges.resolution_rule: the ladder proceeds on its published schedule, but a restructure agreed in a save may reschedule arrears explicitly and in writing - arrears are never waived silently, and suspension of recovery-relevant function on a watch-tier account requires an explicit operator decision first

edges.why_related: retention conversations run under the same ethics as sales: no fear-selling with invented theft threats, and refusal classes stay refused even when the account threatens to leave
edges.risk_of_conflict: a desperate save pitch drifts into dramatized crime risk or quietly accommodates an unlawful tracking request to keep the account

edges.why_related: recording-capable device classes and regulated modules may only be proposed after current rules in the customer's jurisdiction are verified
edges.risk_of_conflict: a dashcam or ELD-module ask goes out with an asserted compliance claim that verification would have contradicted

edges.why_related: the renewal recap may cite only data the audit certified, because one mislabeled vehicle in the recap discredits the whole meeting
edges.risk_of_conflict: an uncertified idle-time trend collapses in front of the customer and turns a continuation decision into a price negotiation

edges.why_related: noisy alerts are a leading generator of tickets, so retuning measurably lowers ticket volume per hundred units
unhandled silent units erode the perceived value of the subscription, and that erosion surfaces months later as churn signals
cause-tagged ticket analysis identifies which alerts generate the most noise, setting the agenda for the next retune session
period-close churn attributions recalibrate the signal weights toward what actually preceded losses in this book
sunset swap campaigns are scheduled so the hardware-refresh conversation lands inside the renewal window, letting one meeting settle both

conflict_axes.name: retention_revenue_vs_lawful_use
conflict_axes.description: MRR pressure - keeping an account, closing an expansion - pulls toward accommodating tracking requests that authorization scope, disclosure, or the covert-tracking bright line prohibit.
poles: keep and grow the recurring revenue
hold the lawful-use and disclosure boundary
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the boundary is absolute: refuse and document out-of-scope requests, and treat disclosure refresh as a precondition of every activation, not a follow-up task

conflict_axes.name: save_depth_vs_support_economics
conflict_axes.description: Concessions deep enough to save a threatened account can pin it below the support-cost floor, converting saved MRR into a permanent loss.
poles: save every account at whatever concession it takes
hold the per-account economics floor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bound every concession by the account's support-cost tier; below the floor the options are restructure or clean release, not discount

conflict_axes.name: billing_firmness_vs_relationship
conflict_axes.description: A published dunning ladder must escalate predictably, yet mechanical escalation on a good account in a seasonal trough converts a collectible into a churn.
poles: enforce the ladder identically for everyone
flex the ladder for account context
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep rung timing published and non-negotiable, but route watch-tier and long-tenured accounts through a human contact rung before any suspension of recovery-relevant function

conflict_axes.name: alert_coverage_vs_alert_fatigue
conflict_axes.description: Every additional alert promises coverage of one more risk, while the accumulated noise trains users to ignore all alerts, including the theft alert that mattered.
poles: alert on everything that could matter
alert only on what a human will act on
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: review firing counts on cadence, kill or repair the top noise sources with the customer present, and protect a small set of always-actionable alerts

conflict_axes.name: truck_roll_vs_remote_resolution
conflict_axes.description: A technician visit fixes almost anything but can consume months of one unit's subscription margin, while remote paths are cheap but stall on genuine hardware faults.
poles: dispatch a technician for certainty
exhaust remote and mail-swap paths first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb the ladder in order, batch visits by yard, and let the account's service tier - not the loudest caller - decide when to skip rungs

conflict_axes.name: monitoring_effort_vs_silent_decay
conflict_axes.description: Proactive health and quality monitoring consumes unbilled hours every week, while skipping it lets dead units and stale data accumulate into renewal-time grievances.
poles: minimize unbilled monitoring overhead
invest monitoring effort ahead of complaints
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: automate the exception lists so human time goes only to true exceptions, and treat every customer-discovered dead unit as a monitoring failure to root-cause

conflict_axes.name: contract_lock_vs_earned_renewal
conflict_axes.description: Long auto-renewing terms protect MRR and subsidy recovery, yet renewals extracted through a notice-window technicality breed resentment that churns hard at the first opening.
poles: rely on term lock-in and auto-renewal
rely on demonstrated value at every renewal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use terms to protect hardware subsidy recovery, but run every renewal as if the lock did not exist - fix-before-ask and an evidence recap either way

conflict_axes.name: expansion_push_vs_account_readiness
conflict_axes.description: Visible whitespace begs to be sold, but an ask landing on an account with dead units, a watch tier, or stale disclosure converts growth pressure into churn pressure.
poles: harvest whitespace as soon as it is visible
expand only into healthy, disclosure-current accounts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: freeze whitespace readiness whenever the health or lawful-use gate fails, and let recorded account events - not quota pressure - trigger the ask

conflict_axes.name: hardware_refresh_timing_vs_cash
conflict_axes.description: Swapping sunset-doomed or aging units early costs hardware cash now, while waiting risks a mass failure event that lands as an emergency at the worst accounts simultaneously.
poles: defer swaps to preserve cash
amortize swaps early across renewal cycles
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: inventory sunset exposure the day a carrier notice lands and spread swap campaigns across the renewal calendar, holding loaners for early failures

conflict_axes.name: reconciliation_rigor_vs_admin_load
conflict_axes.description: Monthly three-way seat reconciliation and unit-level bookkeeping stop margin leaks, but the clerical load competes with installs and support at small-operator scale.
poles: reconcile everything monthly without exception
accept periodic drift to protect field time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the monthly cycle sacred but scope it to deltas since last close; a skipped month is scheduled debt, never silently forgiven

edge_cases.description: A customer asks to add a tracker to an employee's personal vehicle, or to a family member's car, framed as a small favor inside a good account
edge_cases.trigger: an add-unit request whose target vehicle is outside the employer's authorization scope
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse, explain the owner-or-employer-authorized boundary and the disclosure requirement, document the refusal with its trigger, and offer the lawful alternative of tracking only company-owned assets

edge_cases.description: A cellular carrier announces a network-generation sunset that will kill a large slice of the installed base on a published date
edge_cases.trigger: a carrier or vendor lifecycle notice naming modem classes present in the book
edge_cases.mitigation: inventory affected units immediately, spread swap campaigns across the renewal calendar with loaners for early failures, and fold the hardware refresh into each renewal conversation as a mechanism-explained change

edge_cases.description: A fleet account sells a third of its vehicles in a downturn and asks to shed the corresponding subscriptions mid-term
edge_cases.trigger: a fleet downsizing event colliding with contracted unit counts
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a restructure case, not a breach fight: deactivate seats promptly so leaks do not compound, restructure the term to the surviving fleet with any subsidy balance handled explicitly, and record the account as a shrink-to-fit watch case with winback potential

edge_cases.description: Devices report perfectly for months while no human at the account logs in or opens a report
edge_cases.trigger: engagement telemetry showing zero consumption against green device health
edge_cases.mitigation: classify as a zombie account, schedule a re-onboarding touch that reconnects the platform to a live workflow need, and do not let the account reach its renewal window in that state

edge_cases.description: The fleet manager who championed the system and ran the platform leaves the customer
edge_cases.trigger: champion departure detected via bounced contact, changed signatures, or the customer's own announcement
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the account the week it happens, offer successor training as a standard service touch, and rebuild a second engagement contact so the platform is never one person deep again

edge_cases.description: An OBD unit shows a repeating pattern of power-loss events that looks like a driver unplugging it
edge_cases.trigger: power-event telemetry with gaps correlated to one vehicle's shifts
edge_cases.mitigation: report the data gap factually to the employer as a device-continuity issue, verify disclosure was actually made to that driver before anything else, and leave workforce discipline entirely to the employer

edge_cases.description: The platform vendor raises wholesale seat pricing effective mid-term while customer retail prices are locked to contract
edge_cases.trigger: a wholesale price-change notice landing inside active customer terms
edge_cases.mitigation: quantify the margin compression from the operator's own numbers, honor locked terms to their end, and reprice at each renewal with the wholesale movement explained as a mechanism rather than smuggled in

edge_cases.description: A customer disputes the invoice claiming they are being billed for more units than they operate
edge_cases.trigger: an invoice dispute naming specific vehicles or counts
edge_cases.mitigation: freeze dunning escalation on the disputed amount, reconcile the three counts for that account line by line, credit genuine ghost units without argument, and close the turnover-intake gap that created them

edge_cases.description: Battery asset trackers ping on schedule but report stale or drifting positions from inside metal yards and equipment stacks
edge_cases.trigger: plausibility checks showing motionless assets with jittering coordinates or last-known-fix flags
edge_cases.mitigation: distinguish fix quality from device health in the audit, mark affected assets with a location-confidence note before any report cites them, and route persistent cases toward re-siting or antenna guidance from the install practice

edge_cases.description: A customer requests driver-facing dashcams with audio, and the consent and recording rules for in-cab capture in their jurisdiction are unclear
edge_cases.trigger: an expansion ask involving a recording-capable device class
edge_cases.mitigation: pause the proposal until current in-cab recording and consent rules are verified in the customer's jurisdiction, require refreshed driver disclosure covering cameras and audio explicitly, and configure only what the verification supports

edge_cases.description: An account deep in arrears asks for continued location access during dunning because a vehicle was just stolen
edge_cases.trigger: a theft-recovery request colliding with a suspension rung of the dunning ladder
edge_cases.mitigation: keep recovery-relevant location function available during the incident regardless of ladder position, document the accommodation, and resume the published ladder once the incident closes - the arrears remain owed

edge_cases.description: A customer's operations cross into a fleet class that may carry ELD or hours-of-service obligations mid-contract, and they ask the reseller to make them compliant
edge_cases.trigger: an operational change - interstate lanes, vehicle weight class, for-hire status - flagged during a review or expansion conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the obligation class, state plainly that applicability must be verified with current rules in their jurisdiction and their counsel or regulator guidance, and scope any module sale to what the verification concludes rather than promising compliance

workflow.action: Stand up the per-unit MRR ledger
workflow.description: Enumerate every active device as one line with plan tier, retail line, wholesale seat cost, activation date, and contract linkage
workflow.gate: every active platform device maps to exactly one ledger line with all revenue and cost fields populated

workflow.action: Write the lawful-use standing guard into account procedures
workflow.description: Record each account's authorization scope and disclosure status, define the refusal classes, and wire the guard's checks into turnover, expansion, and save procedures
workflow.artifact: authorization and disclosure register with refusal protocol
workflow.gate: every account carries current scope and disclosure entries, and the refusal classes with documentation steps are written

workflow.action: Flag regulated classes across the book
workflow.description: Mark each account that may sit in an ELD, hours-of-service, or telematics-privacy obligation class, with the reason and the verification note
workflow.gate: every flag names its obligation class and reason, and no artifact asserts a jurisdiction-specific rule as fact

workflow.action: Configure device-health monitoring across the base
workflow.description: Build the exception list ranked by last-report age with silence windows per device class and failure signatures noted
workflow.gate: silent units surface within their class's silence window and each carries an owner and next action

workflow.description: Check assignment correctness, odometer plausibility, geofence currency, and duplicates per account, and certify which data may be cited
workflow.gate: every account passes the checklist on cadence or carries an open exception with an owner

workflow.description: Score each account on logins, report consumption, and alert response, counting passive channels, and mark single-point-of-engagement risks
workflow.gate: every account has a current engagement score with passive consumption counted before any account is marked disengaged

workflow.action: Establish the remote-first triage ladder and hardware flows
workflow.description: Define the ladder rungs with exit criteria, mail-swap logistics with return capture, truck-roll batching, and the per-path cost mechanism
workflow.gate: every dead-unit path is priced from the operator's own labor numbers and the ladder order with skip criteria is written

workflow.action: Build the contract register and renewal calendar
workflow.description: Register term dates, notice windows, auto-renew clauses, co-terming policy, and subsidy-recovery balances, then derive the calendar backward from notice windows
workflow.gate: no renewal date sits inside its notice window without an owner and a planned motion

workflow.description: Reconcile platform-billed seats, customer-billed units, and physically alive devices, attributing every delta to a cause
workflow.gate: zero unexplained deltas remain and every explained delta carries a cause tag and close-out action

workflow.action: Run the account health review cadence
workflow.description: Assemble device health, engagement, ticket profile, and value events into a tiered brief with one next action per account
workflow.gate: each brief cites only certified data and carries a tier with evidence and a named next action

workflow.description: Prepare before the notice window: fix or own open problems, build the evidence recap, explain any repricing by mechanism, and offer honest term options
workflow.gate: the recap cites only recorded account events, open problems carry dated ownership, and no invented savings figure appears

workflow.action: Close the book-level MRR gate each period
workflow.description: Attribute every movement to unit, account, and cause, overlay support-cost tiers for growth quality, and assign owners to next-period fixes
workflow.artifact: MRR movement ledger with decision pass
workflow.gate: the period closes only when every movement has a cause and every red flag has an owner with a dated action

dominance_rules.rule: The lawful-use and disclosure guard dominates every retention and expansion motion
dominance_rules.rationale: one covert-tracking incident destroys more trust and exposure than any single account is worth
dominance_rules.trigger: any add-unit, transfer, save, or device-class request touching authorization scope or disclosure
dominance_rules.action: block the activation until scope and disclosure are verified current, and refuse and document requests in the covert-tracking classes

dominance_rules.rule: Jurisdiction verification dominates any compliance-touching claim or module sale
dominance_rules.rationale: ELD, hours-of-service, and telematics-privacy rules are jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific and drift under the book
dominance_rules.trigger: a renewal, expansion, or support answer that would lean on a compliance statement
